card.title: 51st RECON
card.text: When the enemy HQ gains defense, this unit gets equal attack.
card.flavorText: The 51st Reconnaissance Regiment was a unit of the 51st Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division was formed in 1940 and it was transferred to Guangdong in China in 1941. At the time a detachment was used for rearguard duties during the Battle of Hong Kong. In 1942 the 51st Division was transferred to Rabaul in Papua New Guinea as part of the 18th Army. In 1943 it was ordered to the city of Lae in New Guinea,  but on the way its convoy was intercepted by Allied aircraft and only 2,000 of 6,900 troops reached Lae. The division eventually regrouped in the Salamaua area, in the northern eastern coastline of Papua New Guinea. It took part in the Salamaua–Lae campaign which ended in a defeat against the US and Australian forces. The 51st Division retreated from Lae in September 1943 and experienced extreme hardship in the process, losing equipment and suffering from starvation. Lacking weapons and ammunition after their retreat, most of the remaining 51st Division soldiers were unable to participate in combat, except for one company from the 102nd Infantry Regiment which fought at Finschhafen. From 1944 to 1945, the 51st Division's primary struggle was against starvation, and only a small fraction of its soldiers survived until Japan's surrender in August 1945.
